headline: Alex Cora says no to Philly as the Hub waits for next winter move
morning_brew: Quiet day in the Hub, which reminds me of a night back in 2013 when the whole city felt like it was holding its breath. I was sitting in Section thirty-six at Fenway for that ALCS game, and when David Ortiz stepped up and cleared the bullpen fence, the guy next to me, a total stranger, grabbed me in a bear hug so tight my fourteen-dollar Bud Light went flying all over his jacket. We didn't even know each other's names, but for that one moment, when the park shook like an earthquake, we were brothers. Those are the nights that keep us coming back, even through the long, quiet October days when the dust is settling on another season.

It is a bit of a weird feeling not having a game to sweat through, but maybe it is for the best. With Alex Cora officially turning down the Phillies to take 2027 off, the rumors about him heading elsewhere can finally cool off. I respect his run here, but this team needs a jolt, and while ownership is keeping their cards close to the vest regarding the analytics philosophy, at least the air is cleared on the managerial front. I am just looking for a team that plays with that same fire I saw back in the 2013 postseason, because watching this squad navigate a transition period is enough to make any townie pull their hair out.

We will be back at it soon enough, and the sports calendar is already turning toward the hardwood and the ice. The Bruins have a date with Utah at the Garden on Thursday, and the Pats are prepping for the Raiders this Sunday in Foxborough. No baseball tonight, which is probably a mercy for my blood pressure, but I will be spending the time stewing over what this roster needs to look like for next spring. It is gonna be a long winter if we do not start seeing some real movement, but for now, I am just gonna enjoy the silence before the next storm.

news_digest.headline: Report: Alex Cora again declines chance to manage Phillies
news_digest.dans_take: Cora is taking 2027 off, and honestly, the front office has enough to worry about without a managerial search dragging into the holidays.
